target.title: Intermittent document export delays
target.frame: A hosted document service exports customer workspaces overnight. Median export time is stable, but roughly one in twenty exports now takes more than an hour instead of ten minutes. Export traces include queue entry, worker start, object reads and archive upload; trace coverage differs across worker versions. Customers cannot be asked to rerun large exports during business hours. The engineering team must plan a safe investigation and choose the next deployment action.

instrument.state: Several plausible explanations can account for an uncertain situation, and available evidence may fit more than one of them.
instrument.operation: State the competing explanations explicitly, evaluate each item of evidence against all of them, emphasize evidence that is inconsistent with particular explanations, and test the sensitivity of the resulting comparison to uncertain evidence or assumptions.
instrument.signal: The evidence forms a comparative pattern of consistency and inconsistency across the competing explanations, with some items discriminating among them more strongly than others.
instrument.inference: Explanations with greater important inconsistency can be weakened or eliminated, leaving a smaller set of alternatives that better survives the observed evidence.
instrument.limit: Missing hypotheses, dependent or unreliable evidence, subjective consistency judgments, poor assessment of diagnosticity, and shared assumptions can make the comparison misleading. Surviving contradiction is not proof that the remaining explanation is true.

mapping.state: Act on existing export records and traces, distinguishing the stable median from the reported roughly one-in-twenty exports exceeding an hour. Compare explicit, potentially coexisting explanations: queue congestion or worker shortages; worker-version regressions; slow or retried object reads; slow archive uploads; and workspace size or composition differences. Treat these as hypotheses, not findings. Trace coverage varies by worker version; availability of comparable timestamps, workload metadata and resource metrics remains uncertain.
mapping.operation: First examine existing slow and ordinary overnight exports without requesting customer reruns. Where available, compare exports with similar workspace size, object count, execution window and worker version; retain unmatched cases with their limitations. Separate queue wait, worker execution, object-read and upload durations only where trace semantics permit. Build an evidence-by-hypothesis matrix, marking each item consistent, inconsistent or unknown for every explanation and recording reliability and diagnostic value. Prioritize contradictions over counts of supporting items: for example, reliably short queue waits would weaken queue congestion as the direct source of an hour-long export. Avoid treating nested spans or multiple symptoms of one event as independent evidence. Repeat the comparison excluding incomplete traces, varying uncertain phase boundaries, stratifying by version and workload, and considering combined causes. If existing evidence cannot discriminate, propose a small canary deployment adding missing phase timing and coverage metadata, with bounded sampling and logging overhead and no document contents. Use normal overnight traffic; introduce controlled test exports only if representative test data and spare capacity are established. Before deployment, define acceptable instrumentation overhead, error rate, completion rate and tail-delay bounds against comparable baseline traffic. Halt expansion and revert the canary if those bounds are breached or monitoring cannot enforce them. Expand a targeted mitigation only when reliable discriminating evidence favors its mechanism and the canary meets those bounds; otherwise retain the current deployment and gather the specific missing evidence.
mapping.signal: Look for comparative patterns rather than a single suspicious trace. Long queue waits with ordinary post-start durations would favor queue-related delay and weaken downstream-only explanations. Ordinary queue waits followed by prolonged read or upload phases would discriminate in the opposite direction, provided those phases are measured comparably. A version association that persists within comparable workloads and execution windows would support a version-related hypothesis; an association that disappears after accounting for coverage or workload would weaken it. These are proposed observations, not results. Record whether the ranking changes when uncertain evidence is removed and whether the canary changes the predicted phase and overall tail without increasing failures or unfinished exports.
mapping.inference: Weaken explanations that conflict with reliable, diagnostically important observations; eliminate one only within the scope where its necessary prediction was adequately tested. Use the surviving alternatives to choose the next deployment: a bounded mitigation or rollback canary when evidence supports a specific mechanism, an instrumentation canary when observability is the main obstacle, or no behavioral change when uncertainty or operating risk remains too high. A successful mitigation canary would support expanding that action within tested conditions, while leaving open alternative explanations for the improvement. If reliable observations contradict every listed explanation, expand the hypothesis set before choosing a behavioral change.
mapping.limit: Missing spans are unknown evidence, not proof that a phase was fast. Incomplete exports may be absent from completed-export samples and must be accounted for where records permit. Version, workload and overnight load may be confounded; overlapping spans, inconsistent clocks, retries and dependent measurements can distort comparisons. Rare delays require enough comparable exposure to make absence informative, so a short clean canary cannot establish resolution. Specify the observation window and required exposure before judging it; if exposure or coverage is inadequate, report the result as inconclusive and continue only within the safety bounds. Subjective consistency judgments, omitted causes and shared assumptions may leave the ranking wrong. Surviving contradiction does not prove a cause, and instrumentation or test workloads may change the behavior being investigated.

component.value: Each evidence item should be assessed against every candidate explanation as consistent, inconsistent or unknown.
component.scope: The prescribed comparison includes all listed alternatives and permits unknown assessments.

provenance.rationale: The span directly specifies the comprehensive comparison and its three assessment categories.
